meta.title: Global product security control set
meta.note: One control set, run once, mapped to six regimes. Coverage shows how far each regime requires the control: Strong means the regime requires essentially this control; Partial means it requires part of it or only discloses it; Weak means it touches it indirectly or only at a higher voluntary label tier; None means not required. JC-STAR is rated at STAR-1 and CLS at Levels 1-2, with higher-tier references noted. US Cyber Trust Mark ratings rest on the NIST IR 8425 capabilities and the FCC 24-26 declarations, because the programme's final technical requirements were not adopted at 28 Oct 2026. Ratings are indicative judgements for programme design, not legal advice or a statement of conformity.
footnotes: Source "kb": CRA mappings rest on the engagement knowledge base (reports/sections/07, 08, 09, 10, 13, 14; verification.md) and pack/data/crosswalk.json.

Source "web": non-CRA mappings rest on primary texts opened for this module: legislation.gov.uk (PSTI Act 2022, SI 2023/1007, SI 2025/211, SI 2025/1267 contents), FCC 24-26 in the Federal Register (89 FR 61242) and FCC Public Notice DA 26-75, NIST IR 8425, IPA JST-CR-01-01-2024 and JST-SR-03-01-2026, CSA CCC SP-151-2 v1.4, and legislation.gov.au (Cyber Security Act 2024; F2025L00276). Status points come from regulator releases and trade press, cited in paper.md.

Not verified: the commencement date of SI 2025/1267; the full US registry data-element list and 47 CFR Part 8 section headings (eCFR not reachable); the NIST IR 8425 deletion sub-outcome; JC-STAR STAR-2 intake; Australian civil penalty amounts.

coverage_scale.label: Strong
coverage_scale.meaning: The regime requires essentially this control; meeting the regime's test proves this control for that market.

coverage_scale.label: Partial
coverage_scale.meaning: The regime requires part of the control, requires disclosure rather than the property, or applies it only to some products.

coverage_scale.label: Weak
coverage_scale.meaning: The regime touches the topic indirectly, or only at a higher voluntary label tier.

coverage_scale.label: None
coverage_scale.meaning: Not required by the regime; the control is driven by other markets.

frameworks.name: EU Cyber Resilience Act
frameworks.full_name: Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 (Annex I Part I and II; Arts 13-14)
frameworks.status: In force 10 Dec 2024; Art 14 reporting since 11 Sep 2026; full application 11 Dec 2027
frameworks.relation_to_cra: The baseline. Every control is sized first against the CRA because it is the broadest regime: all products with digital elements, B2B and B2C, 13 product properties, 8 lifecycle duties, Art 13 and Art 14.
frameworks.reuse: Annex VII technical file is the master evidence store; the EU declaration, SBOM, CVD policy and support-period rationale feed every other regime.
frameworks.gaps: No security label or public product registry; no national-security supply-chain screening; third-party testing only for Annex III Class I where no harmonised standard, common specification or substantial-level EU certification scheme is applied in full (Art 32(2)), Class II and Annex IV.

facts.Scope: All products with digital elements made available in the EU whose intended or foreseeable use includes a data connection; remote data processing the product depends on (Art 3(2)).
facts.Products: Hardware and software, consumer and business; Annex III important (Class I/II) and Annex IV critical categories.
facts.Conformity route: Module A self-assessment by default; B+C or H with a notified body for Class I unless a harmonised standard, common specification or substantial-level EU certification scheme is applied in full (Art 32(2)); Class II via B+C, H or an Art 27(9) scheme (Art 32(3)); critical products per Art 32(4); FOSS may self-assess with public technical documentation (Art 32(5)).
facts.Labelling: CE marking (Arts 29-30) and EU declaration of conformity (Art 28); no security label.
facts.Reporting: Actively exploited vulnerabilities 24 h / 72 h / final report 14 days after a fix; severe incidents 24 h / 72 h / final report 1 month after the incident notification, via ENISA SRP to the coordinator CSIRT (Art 14).
facts.Penalties: Up to EUR 15m or 2.5% of worldwide turnover, whichever is higher (Art 64(2)); EUR 10m or 2% (Art 64(3)); EUR 5m or 1% (Art 64(4)). Micro and small enterprises are exempt for missed 24-hour deadlines (Art 64(10), as corrected by OJ L, 2025/90555).
facts.Dates: In force 10 Dec 2024; Art 14 from 11 Sep 2026; notified-body chapter 11 Jun 2026; everything else 11 Dec 2027.

frameworks.name: UK PSTI product security regime
frameworks.full_name: PSTI Act 2022 Part 1 and SI 2023/1007, as amended by SI 2025/211 and SI 2025/1267
frameworks.status: In force 29 Apr 2024; vehicles excepted from 25 Feb 2025; JC-STAR and CLS deemed-compliance amendment (SI 2025/1267) made late 2025, commencement not confirmed
frameworks.relation_to_cra: A strict subset of the CRA on three points (default passwords, how to report security issues, published support period), plus a statement of compliance that must accompany the product.
frameworks.reuse: The CRA password, CVD-policy and support-period controls satisfy Schedule 1 if worded to the PSTI tests; EN 303 645 provisions 5.1-1, 5.1-2, 5.2-1 and 5.3-13 give deemed compliance (Sch 2).
frameworks.gaps: Statement of compliance in the Schedule 4 format; support period shown alongside price on own websites (Sch 1 para 3(5)); 10-year retention of statements; English-language, no-personal-data reporting route.

facts.Scope: UK consumer connectable products (Act ss.4-6): internet- or network-connectable products made available to consumers in the UK.
facts.Products: Smartphones, smart home, wearables, routers and similar; excepts desktops, laptops, non-cellular tablets, EV charge points, medical devices, smart meters, certain vehicles (Sch 3).
facts.Conformity route: Self-declared; deemed compliance via ETSI EN 303 645 or ISO/IEC 29147 provisions (Sch 2), and, under SI 2025/1267, a valid JC-STAR STAR-1 or CLS label.
facts.Labelling: No label. Statement of compliance must accompany the product (Act s.9; reg 7; Sch 4).
facts.Reporting: No authority reporting duty. Duties to investigate and act on compliance failures and inform the enforcement authority (Act ss.10-11).
facts.Penalties: Greater of GBP 10m or 4% of qualifying worldwide revenue (Act s.38); daily penalty up to GBP 20,000 (KB); compliance, stop and recall notices (ss.28-30).
facts.Dates: Regulations made 14 Sep 2023; in force 29 Apr 2024; SI 2025/211 from 25 Feb 2025; UK-Japan and UK-Singapore recognition effective 1 Jan 2026.

frameworks.name: US Cyber Trust Mark
frameworks.full_name: FCC IoT Labeling Program, Report and Order FCC 24-26, PS Docket 23-239 (47 CFR Part 8); criteria based on NIST IR 8425
frameworks.status: Voluntary. Rules effective 29 Aug 2024; launched 7 Jan 2025; UL withdrew as Lead Administrator 19 Dec 2025; ioXt selected 13 Apr 2026; no labelled products and technical requirements not finalised as at 28 Oct 2026
frameworks.relation_to_cra: Outcome criteria (NIST IR 8425) sit inside the CRA's Annex I; the programme adds third-party lab testing, a label with a QR code to a public registry, and national-security eligibility declarations.
frameworks.reuse: CRA design evidence (access control, data protection, update, logging) answers the IR 8425 capabilities; the support period and CVD policy feed the registry entry.
frameworks.gaps: Covered List, Entity List and debarment declarations under penalty of perjury; accredited CyberLAB test report; CLA certification; label and registry data; renewal. Final technical standards are still to be put out for comment.

facts.Scope: Consumer wireless IoT products (intentional radiators with a network interface), including companion apps and cloud the product needs.
facts.Products: Cameras, voice assistants, appliances, fitness trackers, garage-door openers, baby monitors; excludes FDA medical devices, motor vehicles, wired-only, enterprise and industrial products, Covered List equipment.
facts.Conformity route: Test by an accredited lab (CyberLAB, CLA-run or in-house), certification by a Cybersecurity Label Administrator accredited to ISO/IEC 17065.
facts.Labelling: FCC IoT Label: the Cyber Trust Mark plus a QR code to a public registry (support period, whether updates are automatic, default-password and secure-configuration guidance).
facts.Reporting: No authority reporting. Applicant declares it will find critical vulnerabilities and issue updates until the registry support end date (FCC 24-26 para 27).
facts.Penalties: Authorisation may be terminated if disclosures are not cured within 20 days (para 28); other FCC enforcement may apply. Declarations are under penalty of perjury.
facts.Dates: Adopted 14 Mar 2024; effective 29 Aug 2024; launch 7 Jan 2025; CLA window 27 Jan-24 Feb 2026; ioXt Lead Administrator 13 Apr 2026; FCC opened a label-design, renewal and post-market proceeding in late Oct 2026.

frameworks.name: Japan JC-STAR
frameworks.full_name: IPA Security Requirements Conformity Assessment and Labelling Scheme for IoT products; STAR-1 criteria JST-CR-01-01-2024
frameworks.status: Operating since 25 Mar 2025 (STAR-1 self-declaration); STAR-3 requirements for communication equipment and network cameras published 2026; STAR-2 intake announced from Jan 2026, not confirmed; 80 companies and 1,500+ models labelled by 31 Mar 2026
frameworks.relation_to_cra: The 16 STAR-1 requirements are a subset of CRA Annex I, with sharper test thresholds (password length, persistence after power loss). STAR-3 adds SBOM, secure boot, logging and third-party penetration testing for government and infrastructure buyers.
frameworks.reuse: CRA access-control, update, data-protection, attack-surface and deletion evidence answers STAR-1 S1.1-01 to S1.1-16; STAR-1 now also gives UK PSTI deemed compliance and CLS Level 1 recognition.
frameworks.gaps: Label application and fee per product; 2-year label validity with extension; product page on the IPA list; the STAR-1 password-length rule; STAR-3/4 third-party evaluation for procurement markets.

facts.Scope: IoT products that communicate over IP, voluntary; government procurement use planned (timing undecided).
facts.Products: All IoT categories at STAR-1; STAR-2 and above by product type, first network cameras and communication equipment.
facts.Conformity route: STAR-1 and STAR-2 self-declaration with checklist to IPA; STAR-3 and STAR-4 evaluation by an IPA-approved third-party body.
facts.Labelling: JC-STAR label with QR code to the IPA product page (status, security contact); valid 2 years, extendable.
facts.Reporting: No authority reporting; vendor must publish a vulnerability disclosure policy (S1.1-05) and provide update support while the label is valid.
facts.Penalties: Label withdrawal or revocation (IPA status list); no statutory fines identified.
facts.Dates: Operation from 25 Mar 2025; first labels May 2025; UK PSTI recognition 1 Jan 2026; Singapore CLS recognition 1 Jun 2026.

frameworks.name: Singapore CLS(IoT)
frameworks.full_name: CSA Cybersecurity Labelling Scheme for IoT; CCC SP-151-2 Scheme Specifications v1.4 (Apr 2025)
frameworks.status: Operating since 2020; four levels; recognised by Finland, Germany, Korea, UK (from 1 Jan 2026) and Japan (from 1 Jun 2026)
frameworks.relation_to_cra: Level 1 equals the PSTI three; Level 2 adds the ETSI EN 303 645 mandatory provisions; Levels 3 and 4 add lifecycle provisions, binary analysis and penetration testing. All sit within CRA Annex I.
frameworks.reuse: One EN 303 645 assessment serves CLS Level 2, PSTI deemed compliance and much of the CRA Annex I file.
frameworks.gaps: CLS application and label per product; lab binary analysis (Level 3) or penetration test (Level 4).

facts.Scope: Consumer IoT, first Wi-Fi routers and smart home hubs, now all consumer IoT categories.
facts.Products: Consumer IoT devices; home-gateway variant references ETSI TS 103 848.
facts.Conformity route: Levels 1-2 declaration reviewed by a test lab and CCC; Level 3 adds binary analysis; Level 4 adds black-box penetration testing.
facts.Labelling: CLS(IoT) label at the level achieved, awarded by CCC.
facts.Penalties: False declarations handled under Publication #1 chapter 15.1 (not read).
facts.Dates: Launched 2020; spec v1.4 Apr 2025; UK MoU 22 Oct 2025, effective 1 Jan 2026; Japan MoC 18 Mar 2026, effective 1 Jun 2026.

frameworks.name: Australia smart-device standard
frameworks.full_name: Cyber Security Act 2024 Part 2 and Cyber Security (Security Standards for Smart Devices) Rules 2025
frameworks.status: In force for products manufactured on or after 4 Mar 2026
frameworks.relation_to_cra: Mirrors UK PSTI: no universal default passwords, a reporting route with acknowledgement and status updates, and a published support period with an end date; plus a statement of compliance.
frameworks.reuse: The PSTI controls and statement template carry over with Australian fields (authorised representatives in Australia; 5-year retention).
frameworks.gaps: Australian statement of compliance supplied with the product (Act s 16; Rules s 9); support period must be expressed with an end date (Sch 1 cl 4(3)).

facts.Scope: Consumer-grade relevant connectable products for personal, domestic or household use (Rules s 8).
facts.Products: Excepts desktops, laptops, tablets, smartphones, therapeutic goods and road vehicles (Rules s 8(1)(b)).
facts.Conformity route: Self-declared statement of compliance; examination powers (Act s 23).
facts.Labelling: No label; statement of compliance accompanies the product.
facts.Penalties: Compliance, stop and recall notices (Act ss 17-19); public notification of non-compliance with a recall notice (s 20); civil penalty amounts not verified.
facts.Dates: Act assent 29 Nov 2024; Rules registered 4 Mar 2025; standards apply from 4 Mar 2026.

requirements.title: Product security governance and secure development lifecycle
requirements.summary: A product security policy with a named accountable executive, and one secure development lifecycle applied to every product line from design to end of support.
requirements.evidence: Product security policy and SDL standard with RACI; per-release SDL gate record generated by the pipeline (see E1).
requirements.strictest: CRA: the lifecycle must deliver risk-appropriate security across design, development and production.

requirements.title: Product cybersecurity risk assessment
requirements.summary: A documented risk assessment per product family that states, item by item, which security properties apply and why any do not, updated through the support period.
requirements.evidence: Risk assessment per product family with Annex I applicability table and residual-risk register (Annex VII point 3).
requirements.strictest: CRA: documented, product-level, with a justification for each non-applied requirement.

requirements.title: Regime scope and product classification register
requirements.summary: One register listing every product, its markets, the regimes that apply, any exception relied on, its CRA class and its conformity route.
requirements.evidence: Portfolio applicability register with legal basis per row, reviewed quarterly (feeds E3 classification).
requirements.strictest: CRA: classification decides whether a notified body is needed; PSTI and AU exceptions decide whether a statement is needed.

requirements.title: Third-party component due diligence
requirements.summary: An intake gate for every third-party and open-source component, with security review, known-vulnerability check and recorded decision.
requirements.evidence: Component intake records per component and version, linked to the SBOM.
requirements.strictest: CRA: covers every component, including free open-source software.

requirements.title: Supply-chain eligibility screening (national-security lists)
requirements.summary: Screen the applicant, its affiliates and the product's components against the FCC Covered List, Commerce Entity List, DoD Chinese Military Companies list and federal debarment lists before a US label application, and again on change.
requirements.evidence: Signed screening record per product and supplier, kept with the label application.
requirements.strictest: US CTM only.

requirements.title: Secure-by-default configuration and factory reset
requirements.summary: Ship in a secure default state (optional services off, debug locked, onboarding enforced) and let the user reset to that state.
requirements.evidence: Default-configuration export per release; onboarding and reset test results.
requirements.strictest: CRA: whole default state plus reset.

requirements.title: No universal default passwords
requirements.summary: Every password is unique per device and not derivable from public data or identifiers, or is set by the user at first use.
requirements.evidence: Credential-provisioning design note; test showing no shared or derivable passwords across a production sample.
requirements.strictest: JC-STAR STAR-1 for the length rule; PSTI and AU for the derivation tests. Build to both.

requirements.title: Attack-surface minimisation
requirements.summary: Only the interfaces needed in each state are enabled; debug ports are locked; development tooling is stripped; network services default to deny.
requirements.evidence: Interface inventory per product state; external port scan; debug-lock evidence.
requirements.strictest: CRA and JC-STAR STAR-1 are equivalent in effect.

requirements.title: Exploit mitigation and secure coding
requirements.summary: Memory-safe languages or hardened builds (ASLR, W^X, CFI), sandboxing, privilege separation and input validation.
requirements.evidence: Compiler-flag and binary-hardening scan output per build; fuzzing reports.
requirements.strictest: CRA only.

requirements.title: No known exploitable vulnerabilities at release
requirements.summary: Release gate that correlates the release SBOM with EUVD, CVE/NVD and the CISA KEV catalogue and blocks release unless each finding is fixed or mitigated.
requirements.evidence: Release-gate scan report with KEV status and decisions, per version.
requirements.strictest: CRA: applies at placing on the market and is judged against public databases.

requirements.title: Authentication and access control on every interface
requirements.summary: Every local, network, app and cloud interface authenticates the caller and enforces roles; privileged roles use MFA; unauthorised access is reported.
requirements.evidence: Access-control model per interface; negative test results; alert catalogue.
requirements.strictest: CRA: adds the duty to report possible unauthorised access.

requirements.title: Credential management and brute-force resistance
requirements.summary: Users can change every authentication value; network login resists brute force (rate limiting or lockout); machine credentials expire.
requirements.evidence: Credential-change and brute-force test results.
requirements.strictest: JC-STAR STAR-1: explicit, testable requirements.

requirements.title: Product identification and asset inventory
requirements.summary: Model, hardware and software version visible to the user; type, batch or serial number marked; the manufacturer can identify every logical and physical component.
requirements.evidence: Marking specification; screenshot of version display; component inventory per version.
requirements.strictest: CRA plus IR 8425: physical marking and a component-level inventory.

requirements.title: Confidentiality of data at rest and in transit
requirements.summary: Encrypt relevant data at rest and in transit with approved algorithms and protected keys; no plaintext fallback.
requirements.evidence: Cryptographic inventory; TLS and downgrade test results; key-management design.
requirements.strictest: CRA: covers stored, transmitted and otherwise processed data.

requirements.title: Integrity of software, data and configuration
requirements.summary: Verified boot and signed software, signed configuration, integrity monitoring, and reporting of corruption.
requirements.evidence: Boot-chain and signature test results; corruption-detection test.
requirements.strictest: CRA: also requires reporting of corruption.

requirements.title: Data minimisation
requirements.summary: Collect and process only the data each function needs; telemetry off by default where not needed; defined retention.
requirements.evidence: Data inventory for the default configuration; retention schedule.
requirements.strictest: CRA only (GDPR applies separately).

requirements.title: Secure data deletion and transfer
requirements.summary: Users can permanently remove all data and settings, and transfer data securely where transfer is offered.
requirements.evidence: Write-erase-read test per data type; export test; user instructions.
requirements.strictest: CRA: adds secure transfer; JC-STAR adds the firmware-version check.

requirements.title: Secure update mechanism
requirements.summary: Updates are signed with protected keys, verified before install, protected against rollback, installed atomically with recovery, and persist across power loss.
requirements.evidence: Update design note; signature, rollback and recovery test results.
requirements.strictest: CRA: adds anti-rollback and recovery through the secure-distribution duty.

requirements.title: Automatic updates by default, with user control
requirements.summary: Security updates install automatically by default where applicable, with notification, postponement and a clear opt-out.
requirements.evidence: Default-configuration proof; opt-out and notification UI evidence.
requirements.strictest: CRA: automatic by default is the rule, not a disclosure.

requirements.title: Timely, free security updates kept separate from feature updates
requirements.summary: Fix vulnerabilities without delay, free of charge, with advisory text, and separate security from feature updates where technically feasible.
requirements.evidence: Remediation SLA policy; update release notes with advisory text; pricing terms.
requirements.strictest: CRA: free and without delay.

requirements.title: Defined support period: set, published, never shortened
requirements.summary: Set a support period per product from expected use, publish it with an end date, publish any extension promptly, and never shorten it.
requirements.evidence: Support-period rationale per product; published support-period page with version history.
requirements.strictest: CRA sets the length (5-year floor); PSTI and AU set the publication and no-shortening tests.

requirements.title: Update availability and archive
requirements.summary: Keep every security update available for at least 10 years or the rest of the support period, whichever is longer; mark archived versions with risk warnings.
requirements.evidence: Signed-artefact repository retention policy and index.
requirements.strictest: CRA only.

requirements.title: Software bill of materials
requirements.summary: Machine-readable SBOM per version covering at least top-level dependencies, generated by the build.
requirements.evidence: CycloneDX or SPDX SBOM per release in the evidence store (E1).
requirements.strictest: CRA.

requirements.title: Published vulnerability disclosure policy and reporting contact
requirements.summary: Publish a CVD policy with at least one reporting contact, acknowledgement and status-update timelines, in English, free, with no personal data required, plus a human channel.
requirements.evidence: Public CVD policy page and security.txt; PSIRT procedure; channel test records.
requirements.strictest: PSTI wording (timelines, English, no personal data) plus the CRA human channel.

requirements.title: Vulnerability triage and remediation (PSIRT)
requirements.summary: Severity-tiered triage with internal remediation SLAs, a vulnerability register linked to the risk assessment, and status updates to reporters until resolution.
requirements.evidence: PSIRT procedure; vulnerability register extract; SLA performance report.
requirements.strictest: CRA: remediation duty for all vulnerabilities, not only critical.

requirements.title: Security testing regime
requirements.summary: Threat-driven security testing per release (SAST, fuzzing, scanning) and periodic independent penetration testing, with re-test triggers.
requirements.evidence: Test plan per product; test and pen-test reports per release (Annex VII point 6).
requirements.strictest: CRA for regularity; CTM, JC-STAR STAR-3 and CLS Level 4 for independent testing.

requirements.title: Public security advisories
requirements.summary: Once a fix is available, publish an advisory (description, affected products, impact, severity, remedy) in human-readable form and CSAF, with any delay justified.
requirements.evidence: Advisory index; CSAF files; delay decision records.
requirements.strictest: CRA.

requirements.title: Upstream reporting to component maintainers
requirements.summary: Report vulnerabilities found in third-party components to their maintainers and share fixes, with a licence check.
requirements.evidence: Upstream report log; patch-sharing records.
requirements.strictest: CRA only.

requirements.title: Security event logging and monitoring
requirements.summary: Record security-relevant events (access, configuration and firmware changes) with accurate time, tamper evidence, export, and a user opt-out.
requirements.evidence: Event catalogue; sample logs; opt-out evidence.
requirements.strictest: CRA: logging plus a user opt-out.

requirements.title: Availability and resilience of essential functions
requirements.summary: Essential functions survive denial-of-service, network loss and power loss; the product recovers without reverting to an insecure state.
requirements.evidence: Essential-function list with mitigations; stress, outage and recovery test results.
requirements.strictest: CRA.

requirements.title: Limit impact on other devices and networks
requirements.summary: No amplification, egress control, back-off on retries, no open relays; documented emitters.
requirements.evidence: Emitter inventory; external scans; amplification calculations.
requirements.strictest: CRA only.

requirements.title: Report actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents
requirements.summary: A 24-hour capable case process that files early warnings, notifications and final reports on the ENISA Single Reporting Platform to the coordinator CSIRT.
requirements.evidence: Case records with UTC awareness time and SRP submission receipts (E2 case engine).
requirements.strictest: CRA only.

requirements.title: Inform users of exploited vulnerabilities and incidents
requirements.summary: Tell affected users, in a structured machine-readable format where appropriate, about the vulnerability or incident and the mitigations they can take.
requirements.evidence: User notification templates; delivery logs.
requirements.strictest: CRA.

requirements.title: User security information and instructions
requirements.summary: Plain-language information on secure setup, use, updates, end of support and safe disposal or data erasure, versioned and kept online.
requirements.evidence: Versioned user security guide and Annex II information per product.
requirements.strictest: CRA Annex II content; JC-STAR adds disposal guidance explicitly.

requirements.title: Support end date at the point of sale
requirements.summary: Show the support end date (at least month and year) where the product is offered, alongside the price on the manufacturer's own website.
requirements.evidence: Point-of-sale template and screenshots per channel.
requirements.strictest: CRA for content (month and year); PSTI for placement (beside the price).

requirements.title: Security label and public registry listing
requirements.summary: Apply for and maintain voluntary security labels where the market values them, keep the registry entry accurate, and control label artwork and QR codes.
requirements.evidence: Label register per SKU and market: label ID, level, expiry, registry URL.
requirements.strictest: US CTM: label plus QR registry with prescribed data.

requirements.title: Manufacturer identification and single point of contact
requirements.summary: Manufacturer name, trade mark, postal and electronic contact on the product, packaging or documents, and a single point of contact for vulnerability reporting.
requirements.evidence: Marking specification; contact page.
requirements.strictest: CRA.

requirements.title: Technical documentation and evidence store
requirements.summary: One evidence store per product version holding design, risk, test, SBOM and vulnerability-handling evidence, from which each regime's file is assembled.
requirements.evidence: Annex VII technical file generated per version by the pipeline (E1).
requirements.strictest: CRA.

requirements.title: Declaration of conformity or statement of compliance
requirements.summary: Issue each regime's declaration from the same evidence: EU declaration, UK statement of compliance, US label declaration, JC-STAR self-declaration, CLS declaration, Australian statement.
requirements.evidence: Declaration generator with per-regime templates; signed declarations per product and batch.
requirements.strictest: All regimes require one; formats differ. The CRA declaration is the most demanding (languages, CE marking).

requirements.title: Conformity assessment route and third-party testing
requirements.summary: Choose and run the assessment route each regime requires, from self-assessment to notified body, accredited lab or IPA evaluation body.
requirements.evidence: Route decision per product and regime; certificates and test reports.
requirements.strictest: CRA Class I/II via a notified body; otherwise US CTM (lab test for every product).

requirements.title: Record retention
requirements.summary: Keep declarations, statements and technical files for the longest period any regime requires.
requirements.evidence: Retention schedule tied to each placing on the market.
requirements.strictest: CRA and PSTI: 10 years or the support period, whichever is longer.

requirements.title: Change control, substantial modification and label renewal
requirements.summary: Assess each release for substantial modification and label impact; refresh declarations, registry entries and labels before expiry.
requirements.evidence: Release impact assessment per version; label expiry calendar.
requirements.strictest: CRA for modification; JC-STAR and CTM for fixed renewal cycles.

requirements.title: Corrective action and regulator cooperation
requirements.summary: Investigate suspected non-compliance, correct, withdraw or recall, inform authorities and users, and answer reasoned requests on time.
requirements.evidence: Corrective-action procedure; regulator request log.
requirements.strictest: CRA and PSTI.

mappings.note: Design, develop and produce to an appropriate level of cybersecurity based on the risks; Part II presupposes an operating lifecycle.
Three outcome requirements only; no lifecycle duty.

mappings.refs: FCC 24-26 para 27 (declaration that the applicant 'has taken every reasonable measure to create a securable product')
mappings.note: Implies a process; no SDL requirement in the rules read.
STAR-1 tests product outcomes only.

mappings.refs: CCC SP-151-2 5.2.1, 5.2.3 (Level 3 lifecycle provisions CK-LP-01 to CK-LP-08)
mappings.note: Only at Level 3 and above.
Outcome requirements only.
Justify every Annex I Part I (2) item not applied; one assessment per family allowed (guidance paras 174-177).
Not required.
The baseline is risk-derived by NIST; manufacturers are not asked for their own assessment in the rules read.

mappings.refs: JST-SR-03-01-2026 (STAR-3 N/A conditions justified with evidence)
mappings.note: STAR-3 only.

mappings.refs: CCC SP-151-2 5.2.1 (IMDA IoT Cyber Security Guide)
mappings.note: Level 3 lifecycle only.
Not required.
